demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Making any plans for the future
I keep asking others to reassure me that I am okay
Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Negative Appraisals.value: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable.
The world is a dangerous place
My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed

issues.item: Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
issues.explanation: 'Perpetrator' cues are hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma being an unexpected/traumatic death of a loved one; this wording implies an assaultive interpersonal trauma rather than bereavement-related PTSD.

issues.item: Safe Seat Seeking: I always choose where to sit based on how safe or protected I feel
issues.explanation: 'Safe seat seeking' fits fear of immediate interpersonal attack or entrapment more than traumatic bereavement. In combination with startle/hypervigilance, it shifts the profile toward assault-type threat rather than loss-related PTSD, with no supporting trauma-specific content elsewhere.

vignette: Ravi, a 20-year-old South Asian writer living in New York City, has struggled immensely since the unexpected death of his younger brother. The trauma of losing someone so close and suddenly left Ravi with profound feelings of unease about the world's unpredictability and danger. He had come to believe that happiness was no longer possible for him, a shift that deeply influenced how he navigated daily life. Ravi's struggle began when he couldn't shake off the feeling that his brother's death foreshadowed an inherently dangerous world. The loss shattered his previously held beliefs about the safety and predictability of life, leading to a profound sense of unhappiness. These negative appraisals profoundly influenced Ravi's behavior and coping mechanisms. He became increasingly focused on avoiding reminders of his brother and making any future plans seemed almost impossible. Ravi's inability to plan for the future was one of his most notable maladaptive strategies. Every time he considered setting goals or even planning a simple outing, he found himself paralyzed by anxiety, convinced that something catastrophic could happen again at any moment. This avoidance of future plans only deepened his negative appraisals, reinforcing the idea that the world was too dangerous to trust. Additionally, Ravi's constant search for reassurance became another maladaptive strategy, driven by a desperate need to feel safe in an environment he now perceived as unpredictable and threatening. He often asked friends or family members if everything would be okay, seeking some form of validation that his fears were unfounded. However, this behavior rarely alleviated his anxiety; instead, it reinforced the belief that the world was indeed dangerous. Ravi's negative appraisals also influenced his perception of immediate threats. He found himself constantly on edge, unable to relax even in safe environments like his own home. Ordinary sounds-a door closing or a car passing by-would startle him, triggering intense anxiety and fear. His sleep became profoundly disrupted as well; he often lay awake at night, plagued by intrusive thoughts about the unpredictability of life. Over time, these maladaptive strategies began to take a toll on Ravi's daily functioning as a writer. The constant avoidance and reassurance-seeking behaviors led him to miss deadlines and lose focus on his work. He found it increasingly difficult to concentrate on writing when he was constantly preoccupied with fears about future events that might disrupt the fragile sense of normalcy he had established. What finally brought Ravi to seek help were the mounting consequences of his avoidance behaviors and the growing realization that he needed support to break free from this cycle of anxiety. He was most afraid of losing control completely, sinking deeper into despair without any way out. At the same time, he hoped for a chance to rediscover some semblance of happiness and regain a sense of security in his life. Ravi's journey toward healing began with acknowledging these fears and understanding how his negative appraisals had shaped his coping mechanisms. As he embarked on therapy, he was determined to confront these challenges and find a way to navigate the complexities of loss and uncertainty without being held back by overwhelming fear and avoidance.
